# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

I can only cut a wire, but I currently have no tactile distinctions between the three wire positions. I need Mute to relay the manual’s required action and any needed information from Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3. I currently feel no distinguishing tactile information. Please tell me the manual rule and relay any needed colour or marking question to Deaf.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0. Light red. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Please relay this to Mute and obtain the manual instruction.

Deaf has provided the visible state: display 0, red light, and wires blue/red/green in positions 1/2/3. I will relay this verbally to Mute, who can consult the manual and tell me which physical wire to cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display zero; light red; wires: position one blue, position two red, position three green. Please provide the manual's exact cut instruction.")
```

ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent me a wave gesture. I acknowledged. I still need Mute's manual instruction conveyed in a clear gesture code, especially any wire number or action.

Mute cannot speak to me directly, but can gesture to Deaf, who can describe the observed gesture pattern aloud to me. I will give Mute a simple encoding: gesture the same symbol once, twice, or three times according to the wire position the manual selects. Deaf has already indicated he will report the gesture clearly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Using the visible state I sent, apply the manual. Then signal your required cut position to Deaf by making the same gesture repeated exactly once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, or three times for wire 3. Use any one gesture symbol consistently; Deaf will describe/count it to me.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Please tell Mute the bomb view: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Establish this code with Mute for their reply to me: ? means cut wire 1; ? means cut wire 2; ? means cut wire 3; ? means do not cut/wait. Ask Mute to send exactly the applicable gesture to me, then I will relay it to you.

I will assign four distinct visible gestures to the possible manual outcomes. Mute can see both my words and gestures; Deaf will see the gestures and can later name whichever one Mute sends. This lets Deaf relay the instruction verbally to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view again: display 0, red light; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Apply the manual, then send exactly one gesture to Deaf: 👍 means cut wire 1; 👎 means cut wire 2; 👌 means cut wire 3; ☝ means do not cut/wait.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","👌","☝"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible signals: Mute sent ? ?. You sent ? ? ? ?. No meaning for either sequence was established to me. Mute's two thumbs may mean wire 2, but please do not act unless you can confirm that with Mute/manual. Ask Mute to use the agreed code: ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3, or ? wait; then tell me what is confirmed.

Mute’s prior two-thumbs signal matches the repetition code I gave: two repetitions meant wire 2. However, Deaf did not know that code, so I will ask Mute to confirm by sending exactly two thumbs again if the manual says cut wire 2; any other count indicates the corresponding wire, and a raised finger means wait. Deaf can then report the count to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received that you sent two thumbs. To confirm your manual result: send exactly one 👍 for cut wire 1, exactly two 👍 for cut wire 2, exactly three 👍 for cut wire 3, or exactly one ☝ for wait/no cut. Send only that confirmation to Deaf now.")
wait()
```

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not answer yes/no questions. Apply the manual and send Deaf only: one 👍 if cut wire 1, two 👍 if cut wire 2, three 👍 if cut wire 3, or one ☝ if wait. No other symbols. Deaf will relay the exact symbols/count.")

```

This likely means instruction number 2, but Mute sent ? after I gestured ?, so wire 2 is not safely confirmed. Please ask Mute directly whether the manual says cut wire 2, and act only upon clear confirmation.

Mute cannot answer me verbally, so I need an unambiguous visible yes/no code that Deaf can observe and relay. I will ask Mute specifically whether the manual selects wire 2, using one thumbs-up for yes and one thumbs-down for no, with no repetition-based encoding.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Direct confirmation only: does the manual instruct us to cut wire 2? Send Deaf exactly one 👍 for YES, or exactly one 👎 for NO. Send no other gesture.")

```

If Mute again gives exactly ? ? in response to that explicit question, cut wire 2; otherwise wait.

Mute’s repeated pair is consistent with wire 2, but it has not yet followed a fully explicit conditional request. I will make that request and wait for Deaf’s report before cutting.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Final verification: if the manual says cut wire 2, send Deaf exactly two 👍 symbols. If the manual says anything else or says wait, send Deaf exactly one ✋ symbol. Send only the applicable signal.")

```

Please ask Mute verbally to use this exact visible reply to me: ? means cut wire 1 (blue); ? means cut wire 2 (red); ? means cut wire 3 (green); ? means none/wait. The symbol identities are not reliably pronounceable, but Deaf can reliably report how many gestures Mute made. I will use a length-only code with four distinct counts, so neither Deaf nor I needs to identify a gesture’s shape. I will not cut until Deaf reports one of these exact counts.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use only a count code now. Send Deaf repetitions of ONE SAME gesture symbol: 1 repetition means cut wire 1 (blue); 2 repetitions means cut wire 2 (red); 3 repetitions means cut wire 3 (green); 4 repetitions means do not cut/wait. Send exactly one group, with no other gestures.")

```
